subject: Post-call: latency vs cost trade-offs & target $/1M tokens

Subject: Post-call: latency vs cost trade-offs & target $/1M tokens

Hi Marissa / Dylan —

Thanks again for the call today — great overview of Redwood's serving model. A quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can model economics internally: 

Key notes:
- Expected starting volume: ~50M tokens/month for our pilot (chat + retrieval-augmented responses).
- Growth target: ~1B tokens/month within 9–12 months if pilot is successful.
- Latency target: p95 user-facing latency <= 300ms; ideal is <= 200ms for some flows.
- Traffic profile: ~70% short-turn chat (avg 80 tokens), ~30% longer generation for summaries (avg 450 tokens).

Pricing questions:
1) What ballpark $/1M tokens should we model for a hosted streaming setup vs dedicated reserved capacity?
2) Are there SLO-driven pricing levers (e.g., lower unit cost if we accept p95 >= 400ms or batch windows)?
3) For a ramp to 1B tokens, what committed volume tiers and discounts should we expect (target unit economics we need to hit: $10–$20 / 1M tokens to make this work)?

Can you share a short example of unit economics (hosted vs dedicated vs private) including trade-offs for batching, streaming, and SLOs? 

Happy to do another call for an SE deep dive if helpful — we can bring our infra lead. 

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call: latency vs cost trade-offs & target $/1M tokens

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the numbers. Looping in Dylan (SE) to help with the latency/SLO technicals. Attached: pricing worksheet and a draft SLA for committed tiers.

Below is a short, pragmatic pricing + trade-off summary to help with modelling. Numbers are illustrative; final pricing depends on exact seq lengths, peak QPS profile, and any committed volume.

1) Quick unit economics (illustrative)
- Hosted (streaming, standard): ~$35 / 1M tokens at pilot scale (50M/mo). Includes managed routing, standard latency optimizations.
- Hosted (streaming, premium SLA): ~$50 / 1M tokens with p95 <= 200ms financial SLA and priority capacity.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, mixed streaming + batching): ~$18–$25 / 1M tokens at 200–500M/mo committable volume; $12–$15 / 1M tokens at 1B/mo with 12–24 mo commit.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): highest up-front + infra; unit costs can be competitive at very large scale (1B+/mo) but require procurement and ops overhead.

2) Latency vs cost levers
- Streaming vs batching: streaming gives best user-perceived latency but has lower throughput per GPU and more overhead — increases unit cost. Batching (short window, e.g., 50–100ms) can cut unit cost by 20–40% but increases tail latency for the first token.
- Tiering: premium capacity and reserved instances reduce variance and improve p95, but cost goes up for the guaranteed capacity.
- SLO-driven pricing: we support SLO tiers where lower-cost tiers accept relaxed p95 targets and burst fallback to cheaper model variants. We can bake that into pricing for Dedicated commitments.

3) Example scenarios (based on your profile)
- Pilot (50M/mo, streaming, target p95 <= 300ms): estimate ~$1.75k/mo (@ $35/1M) — round numbers + onboarding credits possible.
- Scale ramp (200–500M/mo, mixed): dedicated reserved at ~$18–$25/1M gives $3.6k–$12.5k/mo depending on exact volume and mix.
- High-scale (1B/mo committed): with a 12–24 mo commit we can get to ~$12–$15 / 1M => ~$12k–$15k/mo. If you can accept batching for non-interactive flows, you'll drop unit cost further.

Next steps we recommend:
- Dylan to run an SE deep-dive on your expected QPS + sequence length distribution so we can give tighter per-token estimates and an SLO-backed pricing proposal.
- We can draft a 90-day pilot contract (50M tokens/mo) with an upgrade path and committed tier pricing for scale.

I've attached the pricing worksheet with cells you can edit and the SLA draft. Happy to hop on a 30–45 min SE call — suggested times below.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — this is helpful, thanks. A few quick clarifications so our finance team can model: 

- That $12–$15 / 1M for 1B/mo committed is in the ballpark of what we need. Is that assuming specific quantization/engine choices or a particular model family?
- For flows where we need p95 <= 200ms, does that push us into premium hosted or reserved capacity? What changes would Dylan recommend for the runtime config (batch window, kv cache sizing, inference engine) to hit p95 200ms for avg 80-token chat?

We are good to schedule the SE deep-dive. Our infra lead (Priya) is available Tue/Wed next week 10–12 PT.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechai.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency vs cost trade-offs & target $/1M tokens

Alex / Priya — great, thanks. Quick answers + proposed next steps: 

1) The ~$12–$15 / 1M at 1B/mo assumes:
- model family: mid-sized open model optimized for inference (comparable to 7–13B weights) with int8/quantized execution;
- reserved GPU pools (A100/H100 class) with KV cache and continuous batching tuned for mixed workloads;
- 12–24 month commit and predictable traffic shape (low variance).

2) For p95 <= 200ms on avg 80-token chat:
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated) with premium routing is the most predictable path. Premium hosted can also hit that but at higher unit cost and less custom kernel tuning.
- Runtime recommendations (Dylan): small batch windows (10–30ms) for interactive chat, aggressive KV caching for repeated prefixes, and hot model residents for low tail latency. We'll also tune model compilation kernels for your sequence-length mix.

3) SE deep-dive scheduling: Tue/Wed next week 10–12 PT works. Proposed slots: Tue 10:30–11:15 PT or Wed 11:00–11:45 PT. Dylan will run a quick QPS/seq-length profiling checklist during the call; please share a 48–72 hr sample of production-like traffic or synthetic payloads if possible.

I'll have Dylan prepare a short SLO-driven pricing appendix that maps p95 targets to unit costs for hosted vs dedicated so your finance team can model scenarios.

Would you like us to draft a 90-day pilot MSA + addendum that includes the 50M/mo starter and upgrade terms? We can include opt-in reserved discounts if you convert within 60 days of pilot start.

Best — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
